title: King Kamehameha V Judiciary History Center

services.name: Self-Guided Tours
services.desc: The Judiciary History Center’s museum is thought-provoking for all audiences. Visitors are welcome to explore the Center on a self-guided tour, Monday through Friday, from 8:00 am until 4:00 pm. Galleries and exhibits explore topics such as the Kapu system, foundations of democracy, land, labor, and economy, the overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom, and martial law during World War II. Learn about Hawaiʻi’s transition from the traditional Kapu system to a modern judiciary, infusing Hawaiian ideals within western institutions. Models of downtown Honolulu, the original courthouse, a juror’s chair, and three justices armchairs illustrate daily life and courthouse operations in the 1850s. Test

explain.meaning: You go on your own with a map or directions, no guide.

blurb: The Judiciary History Center is the permanent education facility and history museum of the Hawaiʻi State Judiciary. Our mission is to interpret and inform the public about the judicial process and Hawaiʻi’s legal history from ka wā kahiko (the past) through kēia au (the present).
